§3§lMonitoring and binding§r
The first right-click binds the Portable Wireless Network Monitor to the current player. Later right-clicks cycle the HUD through Off, Normal and Scientific; sneak-right-click rebinds it to the current player. In inventory or a Baubles slot, it displays the bound grid's EU, instantaneous and average EU/t, and power tier. This quest requires crafting §11§r monitor and ticking the confirmation.

§3§lBattery installation and charging§r
Shapelessly craft the monitor with a compatible GT/IC2 rechargeable battery to install it; the item remains the same monitor. Battery capacity and voltage tier determine its buffer and charging rate, and the new battery's charge enters the buffer. While carried in inventory or a Baubles slot with a partly empty buffer, it requests a full refill every §1200 ticks (10 seconds)§r. The grid pays supplied EU × (§11§r + downlink loss fraction).

§3§lTool charging and battery replacement§r
Compatible electric tools in inventory, armor and Baubles slots charge simultaneously at §11A × battery voltage§r per tool, limited by the remaining buffer. Charge updates preserve held-tool use and mining. Shapelessly craft with a new battery to replace the installed one: the new battery retains its own charge, while the old battery receives the remaining monitor buffer and returns to inventory, or drops if inventory is full. Tips appear on first acquisition and after §110§r and §120 minutes§r of continued possession, for §13§r tips in total.

§3§lCharging status and settings§r
A battery-equipped monitor adds a charging status line: Buffer empty, Standby, Charging and Charging complete. After §11 second§r without new charging demand, Charging complete appears for about §15 seconds§r before Standby; new demand resumes Charging immediately. Use /gtswn hud charge on/off to toggle the charging line; the eu, instant and average subcommands control the energy, instantaneous and average lines. All four lines have configuration options, and commands save their corresponding settings.

§3§lBattery removal and recipe lookup§r
Shapelessly craft a battery-equipped monitor with a GT5U crowbar to remove its battery. The old battery retains the remaining buffer charge and returns to inventory, or drops if inventory is full. NEI provides §12§r crafting-table examples: installing a GT small lithium battery and removing it with a GT5U crowbar. Installation and replacement accept compatible batteries beyond that example. An equipped monitor shows its buffer through GT/IC2 energy tooltips and a charge bar.
